questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car. This way, the driver will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of for the best protection?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another durable material to protect your hands.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made of?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: In Texas, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) level means a person is legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: In Texas, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is legally intoxicated. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to the frame.

questions.explanation: Make your motorcycle easier to see by wearing bright, reflective clothing. Always ride with your headlight on, use turn signals, and use your brake light properly.

questions.question: When using a motorcycle you are not familiar with, what should you do?

options.text: Check that the seat is comfortable.
Assume it is in good condition.
Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride normally since all bikes are the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding an unfamiliar bike, practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn the gear pattern first.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's brake light compare to a car's brake lights?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop to help other drivers notice.

questions.question: Which item is not protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding, such as sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: What should you look for to get the best helmet protection?

options.text: It meets Department of Transportation guidelines.

questions.correctAnswerText: It meets Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no visible damage.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. The best choice is a DOT-approved helmet, eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Why is space around your motorcycle helpful when riding?

options.text: It gives you time to react to hazards.
It hides you from other drivers.
It prevents you from avoiding hazards.
It allows you to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Why should you keep a safe distance behind other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time and space to see and react to hazards.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you room to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of hazards on the road, such as potholes.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer to stop than usual, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance on slippery surfaces. If your motorcycle takes longer to stop, stay farther back from the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What reduces head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. It is your best protection in a crash.

questions.question: How can you lower your risk of a crash?

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Do not look ahead while riding.
Ride in the parts of a lane that are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Why should you ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass?

options.text: It improves what you can see.
It reduces what you can see.
It makes it hard to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It improves what you can see.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to improve your view and be more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: A few minutes and should be done once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and must be done by a mechanic.
Over an hour and only needed if carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Riding faster can increase danger by making them tailgate at higher speed.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: Traffic is less likely to separate a small group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws.
Riders will always try to catch up.
It is hard to keep track of everyone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is less likely to separate a small group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have advantages over large groups. They are easier for other vehicles to pass safely. They are less likely to get separated by traffic or stop lights. There is also less need for slower riders to rush to keep up.
